name: Sleipner CO₂ Storage
description: World's first dedicated offshore CO₂ storage project, separating CO₂ from Sleipner gas production and injecting it into the Utsira saline aquifer since 1996.

name: Snøhvit CO₂ Storage
description: Captures CO₂ from the Melkøya LNG plant and injects it into the Tubåen formation beneath the Snøhvit field; restarted in 2022 after the 2020 plant fire.

name: Northern Lights
description: Europe's first open-access CO₂ transport and storage network; receives liquefied CO₂ at Øygarden and injects it into a North Sea saline aquifer. Phase 1 commissioned 2024/2025.

name: Heidelberg Materials Brevik CCS
description: First commercial-scale carbon capture at a cement plant, capturing CO₂ from the Norcem Brevik kiln for shipment to Northern Lights; captured first CO₂ during its 2025 ramp-up.

name: Hafslund Celsio Klemetsrud CCS
description: Planned CO₂ capture at Oslo's Klemetsrud waste-to-energy plant, originally part of the Longship project and now pursued by Hafslund Celsio with new partners.

name: Tata Chemicals Europe CCS
description: The UK's first commercial industrial carbon capture plant, capturing CO₂ from a gas-fired combined heat and power plant to produce pharmaceutical and food-grade sodium bicarbonate and salt.

name: Net Zero Teesside Power (NZT Power)
description: bp-Equinor gas-fired power station with integrated carbon capture at Teesside; FID taken in late 2024 with construction under way and operation expected around 2028.

name: Net Zero Teesside Industrial Capture
description: Aggregates CO₂ capture from multiple Teesside industrial emitters, including CF Fertilisers, for transport to the Northern Endurance Partnership store.

name: H2Teesside
description: bp's planned large-scale blue hydrogen production facility at Teesside with CO₂ capture, feeding the East Coast Cluster.

name: Northern Endurance Partnership
location: Endurance saline aquifer, North Sea, United Kingdom
description: Offshore CO₂ transport and storage system serving the East Coast Cluster, injecting into the Endurance saline aquifer; FID taken December 2024.

name: EET Hydrogen (HPP1) Stanlow
description: Blue hydrogen production at the Stanlow refinery with CO₂ capture routed to the HyNet cluster; the first plant (HPP1) is under construction.

name: Eni Liverpool Bay CO₂ Storage
location: Liverpool Bay, Irish Sea, United Kingdom
description: Eni's offshore CO₂ storage hub in depleted Irish Sea gas fields, forming the storage arm of HyNet; FID taken October 2024.

name: Viridor Runcorn CCS
description: CO₂ capture at the Runcorn energy-from-waste plant, connecting to the HyNet cluster for transport and storage.

name: Encirc Elton CCS
description: CO₂ capture at the Elton glass manufacturing site as part of the HyNet cluster.

name: Hanson Padeswood CCS
description: Carbon capture at Heidelberg Materials' Padeswood cement works, feeding the HyNet cluster.

name: Acorn CCS
description: Scottish CCS project capturing CO₂ at the St Fergus gas terminal for storage in the Goldeneye/Acorn offshore store; a UK Track-2 project led by Storegga with Shell and Harbour Energy.

name: Viking CCS
description: Harbour Energy-led CO₂ transport and storage cluster in the Humber region, using the Viking depleted gas fields and targeting injection from around 2027.

name: Drax BECCS
description: Bioenergy with carbon capture and storage at the Drax power station, aiming to remove millions of tonnes of CO₂ per year pending government support.

name: Peak Cluster
description: Planned capture network linking cement and lime plants in Derbyshire and Staffordshire to offshore storage.

name: Morecambe Net Zero
description: Spirit Energy's plan to store CO₂ in the depleted Morecambe Bay gas fields.

name: Solent Cluster
description: ExxonMobil-led cluster at Fawley aiming to produce blue hydrogen and capture industrial CO₂ for offshore storage.

name: Medway / Isle of Grain Energy Hub
location: Isle of Grain, Kent, United Kingdom
description: National Grid Ventures' proposal to develop a CO₂ import and storage hub at the Isle of Grain LNG terminal.

name: Porthos
operator: Port of Rotterdam Authority / Gasunie / EBN
description: Rotterdam's CO₂ transport and storage project injecting captured industrial CO₂ into depleted North Sea gas fields; under construction with first injection expected in 2026.

name: Aramis CCS
description: Large-scale CO₂ transport and storage initiative in the Dutch North Sea, aggregating emitters from Rotterdam and beyond for injection from around 2028/2030.

name: L10 CO₂ Storage
description: Planned CO₂ storage in the depleted L10 gas field in the Dutch North Sea, led by Neptune Energy (now Eni).

name: CO2next
description: Liquid CO₂ import, buffer and export terminal at Rotterdam's Maasvlakte enabling flexible CO₂ shipping.

name: Project Greensand
location: Nini West field, Danish North Sea
description: Pioneering cross-border CO₂ storage in Denmark's Nini West field; completed Europe's first cross-border injection pilot in 2023 with full-scale operation planned.

name: Bifrost
description: Ørsted-led offshore CO₂ storage project in the Danish North Sea (Harald field), planned to store around 3 MtCO₂/yr.

name: Norne CO₂ Storage Hub
description: Danish onshore-to-offshore CO₂ storage hub in North Jutland, led by a TotalEnergies consortium, aiming to store CO₂ from around 2030.

name: Climeworks Orca
description: Climeworks' first commercial direct air capture and storage plant at Hellisheiði, capturing about 4,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year using Carbfix mineralisation.

name: Climeworks Mammoth
description: Climeworks' larger direct air capture plant in Iceland, ramping up to about 36,000 tonnes per year with CO₂ mineralised underground by Carbfix.

name: Carbfix Hellisheiði
description: Dissolves CO₂ in water and injects it into basalt at Hellisheiði, where it mineralises into rock; operational since 2014.

name: BECCS Stockholm (Stockholm Exergi)
description: World's first large-scale bioenergy with carbon capture and storage at a district-heating biomass plant, with FID taken in 2025 and biogenic CO₂ removal targeted by 2028.

name: Heidelberg Materials Slite CCS
description: Heidelberg Materials' planned carbon capture at the Slite cement plant on Gotland, Sweden's largest single industrial CO₂ emitter.

name: Preem Lysekil CCS
description: Planned carbon capture at Preem's Lysekil refinery to reduce refinery emissions.

name: Ravenna CCS
description: Eni-Snam joint venture CCS hub in the Adriatic; Phase 1 began injecting CO₂ in 2024, with Phase 2 targeting around 4 MtCO₂/yr of industrial emitters.

name: GeZero (Geseke)
description: Heidelberg Materials' planned full-chain CCS at its Geseke cement plant, capturing CO₂ for transport to North Sea storage.

name: Pycasso CO₂ Storage
description: Teréga and TotalEnergies' planned CO₂ transport and storage hub in south-west France using the depleted Rousse gas field.

name: Dunkerque Industrial CCS
description: Planned industrial CCS in the Dunkirk area, initially targeting ArcelorMittal's steelworks emissions for offshore storage.
